metadata.rawInput: {"command": "cd /work && for t in svg g defs marker rect line circle path text; do o=$(grep -o \"<$t[ >]\" SystemContext.svg | wc -l); c=$(grep -o \"</$t>\" SystemContext.svg | wc -l); s=$(grep -o \"<$t [^>]*/>\" SystemContext.svg | wc -l); echo \"$t: open=$o close=$c selfclosed=$s\"; done"}

part.text:
The image is ready.

**`/work/SystemContext.svg`** — one file per view; the workspace defines exactly one view (`SystemContext`), so that's the only image.

A few notes on how it was produced:

- **Validated first**: the DSL passed Structurizr validation (`OK`), and I pulled the view's exact contents from the official `export-plantuml` / `export-c4plantuml` MCP exports (Patron → Library, "Browses the catalogue through" [HTTPS], left-to-right layout, legend shown).
- **SVG instead of PNG**: this environment has no local renderer (no Java, PlantUML, Graphviz, Python, or Node) and no network route to a remote one (the PlantUML server is unreachable, and the sandbox's `fetch` is blocked). Since you allowed SVG, I generated it directly from the validated model using the standard C4 palette (person `#08427B`, system `#1168BD`), and verified the markup is well-formed.

If you specifically need a PNG, two easy paths: open the SVG in any browser and save/screenshot it, or — if this environment ever gets network access — I can re-run the render through the PlantUML server (I already have the encoded request ready).
